title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: LiteLLM
providers.scope_notes: Covers LiteLLM Proxy (AI Gateway). Self-hosted open-source proxy (MIT) with an Enterprise license gating JWT auth, IP filtering, audit logs and key rotation; all controls are operator config on your own deployment.

controls.name: allowed_ips
controls.what: Only listed client IPs can call proxy endpoints; others get 403.

controls.name: JWT audience/issuer validation
controls.what: JWT_AUDIENCE/JWT_ISSUER or litellm_jwtauth.issuers restrict which tokens are accepted; unset means any token from listed providers is accepted.

controls.name: enable_jwt_auth
controls.what: JWT tokens are only checked when this config setting is on; leaving it unset means JWT auth is not accepted.

controls_unknown: Whether /key/delete and /key/block take effect instantly or after an auth-cache TTL (only SCIM deprovisioning is documented as clearing the cache).
Master key expiry and SCIM token expiry, rotation and revocation steps.
Whether management GET calls (/key/info, /key/list, /spend/logs) are logged anywhere besides server logs.

auth_paths.name: OIDC / JWT-based auth (incl. Kubernetes ServiceAccount tokens)

authentication.summary: With enable_jwt_auth, the proxy accepts IdP-signed JWTs as bearer tokens, validated against configured JWKS URLs; claims map to users, teams and admin scope.

federation.details: Any OIDC issuer with JWKS, including Kubernetes service account tokens. Audience/issuer checks are optional unless configured.

lifetime.summary: Set by the IdP via exp; proxy checks exp

renewal.summary: Client obtains a new JWT from its IdP.

administration.summary: Configured in config.yaml (enable_jwt_auth, JWT_PUBLIC_KEY_URL, JWT_AUDIENCE, litellm_jwtauth.issuers).

sso.details: Tokens are issued by the operator's own OpenID provider, so IdP policy applies at issuance; LiteLLM only verifies signature and claims at use.

sso.ui: config.yaml general_settings: enable_jwt_auth: true; env JWT_PUBLIC_KEY_URL=<IdP JWKS URL>, JWT_AUDIENCE; or litellm_jwtauth.issuers per issuer. IdP MFA/SSO policy applies at token issuance.

expiry.ui: Set token lifetime at the OpenID provider (exp claim); proxy verifies exp on every request

kill.ui: Remove the issuer from JWT_PUBLIC_KEY_URL / litellm_jwtauth.issuers in config, or rotate IdP signing keys; restart the proxy or wait public_key_ttl (default 600s)

log_sources.name: Audit Logs (LiteLLM_AuditLog)
log_sources.notes: Enterprise; on by default with license, else store_audit_logs: true. UI Logs -> Audit Logs; export via audit_log_callbacks (e.g. S3). Retention is your DB.

log_sources.name: Spend logs (LiteLLM_SpendLogs)
log_sources.notes: Per-request rows with key hash; no prompt content by default; can be disabled; retention via maximum_spend_logs_retention_period.

anomaly_cues: Tokens from unexpected issuer when JWT_AUDIENCE/JWT_ISSUER unset

containment.steps: Revoke at the IdP, remove the issuer/JWKS URL from config, or rotate signing keys.
containment.notes: Issued JWTs remain valid until exp unless the issuer is removed; JWKS cached for public_key_ttl.

unknown: Exact log fields for JWT-authenticated requests

calls.reveals: Mint a virtual key with the JWT (shown in docs)

evidence.title: What is stored in the DB
